sources.entry: How to avoid On-Call Burnout the SRE Way

summary.name: How to avoid on-call burnout
summary.one_liner: A Squadcast blog article offering practical advice for reducing on-call stress for engineering teams, covering rotations, vacation handoffs, deploy practices, incident context, SLOs and runbooks.
use_cases: Designing a fair on-call rotation across an engineering team
Handing off on-call shifts during vacation or emergencies
Setting a no-deploy policy for weekends and holidays
Adding context to incidents to lower MTTR
Using SLO and error budget trends to anticipate incidents
Building runbooks and playbooks for common incidents
summary.what_it_does: The article argues that on-call stress reflects system health and team culture, and recommends expanding on-call rotations so load is shared. It describes overriding schedules via automated incident tags and handing off shifts through a "Vacation Mode" for planned or unplanned absence. It suggests a no-deploy practice for weekends and holidays, with engineers available for at least a working day after deploys. It also covers adding context to incidents through tags, severity levels and alert integrations, and using SLO and error budget trends plus runbooks and remediation actions to respond proactively.
notable: Vacation Mode for handing off on-call shifts for planned and unplanned time off
No Deploys practice for weekends and holidays, adapted from No Deploy Fridays
Uses SLO and error budget correlation to predict customer-impacting downtime
Promotes runbooks and CI/CD-integrated remediation actions within the incident platform
caveats: Page is a blog article with promotional sections for SolarWinds Incident Response and Squadcast; product features are described only in general terms
Mobile apps are mentioned only in a closing promotional line; no pricing is stated
